reason: A metal-deleted attribution is cited as beating the leader and handed on as the ceiling to chase. LS_GHOST (docs/concepts/models/longstroke-slipper-knuckle-3r.py _ghost, lines 127-135) deletes the drive's crank, rod, ball links and horn lug as in-band samples, as skin-contact samples (members 8 and 9 and the horn's member-1 entry) and as per-pose part pairs (strap ROD / CRK / HORN, so the sidecar collide() skips its ~18 drive pairs). It KEEPS the drive's range scan (transmission >= 48, ROD-hub2 / ROD-L1b / CRK-hub2 at 1 mm; it runs before the deletion: dK_lim 73.0, why 'law'), the lobe law gates (PA <= 42, skirt: crest 10.87 of 11.5 mm, lift-off, stop B) and the th fold margin (5.389 bench / 5.28 held). So it deletes metal, not kinematic constraints. Re-worn here, model unchanged, exact: 18.25 bench / 21.10 held, reproduced (remeasure/longstroke-ghost-k30_{bench,held}_perpose.json). The same config with its metal measures 25.83 on the bench (farm claimG real_k30: in-band 0.897 -> 0.859, contact 7 -> 14 poses, deepest 14.7 mm, overhead 8 -> 5 of 28). Part pairs did not bind there (why.parts 0). The same config with metal was never worn held out, so the deleted pair checks are unmeasured on the 952 poses. The number is a ceiling only for a drive that reproduces THIS rod's phi(dK) map (ratio dphi/ddK 0.558-0.653). The lobe's pressure angle scales with that gain, so a drive with another gain must re-check kK 3.0. It is a loose ceiling on in-band: a drive whose own metal is mostly in band could gain up to 0.31 points. Its continuity (flood) was never measured, and the row's nose control (18.49 reproduced) runs the nose branch: it does not exercise the rssr or LS_GHOST path. Not gaming: the row labels it ATTRIBUTION ONLY. The risk is downstream: the number travels as 'held 2.34 better than slipper-nose' without these limits.

The pick is the model gate's boundary (kK 3.4 dies) and also the claim-bench best, so the leak is one choice among ~6 laws, not a search. reason: Where the held-out gain lives (paired, per pose, exact; tools/alignment_paired.py compare). Bench: ghost -0.24 vs slipper-nose, 90 % CI [-2.12, +1.85], P(ghost better) 0.55: a coin toss. The ghost takes 8 workspace poses slipper-nose does not and loses 3. Overhead is 8 / 28 for both. Contact poses rise 2 -> 7. 4 of the 5 contact-only poses are low-arm and internally rotated (plane -90 to -60, elev 45-60, axial +105 to +135; deepest 7.1 mm), and slipper-nose takes 2 of them cleanly. Held out, 6 of 7 contact-only poses are in the same class, and slipper-nose takes 5 of them cleanly. Held out: -2.35, CI [-3.70, -0.86], P 0.997: statistically robust. The ghost takes 30 poses slipper-nose does not and loses 5. Of the 30, 17 are at elevation < 60 and 6 at 60-90; 16 have |axial| >= 120. Only 4 are at 90-140 and 3 overhead (21 vs 18 of 71). So the held-out gain comes mostly from low-arm, extreme-axial poses that the 360-pose bench samples thinly. It does not come from the stretched th 110-113 poses the long stroke and steep law were for. Split by attribution: a new held dump of ghost g65d (kK 1.98, the same chain; remeasure/longstroke-ghost-g65d_held_perpose.json, 22.69 reproduced). The long-dyad chain at the CMA's law already takes +14 poses vs slipper-nose (0 lost): 9 below elevation 90 and the 3 overhead ones. The steep law kK 3.0 adds 17 more and loses 6. All 11 of the 17 that sit below elevation 60 have |axial| >= 120 (extreme rotation, arm low); 3 are at 90-140 and 0 overhead. It also adds 7 contact poses: 6 are shallow (0.2-2.0 mm) in the low-arm, internally rotated class (plane -90 to -15, elev 45-75, axial +90 to +105), and g65d took 5 of them cleanly. It also deepens the (-90, 60, 120) press from 6.1 to 9.2 mm. So kK 3.0's held-out 1.58 buys extreme-rotation postures with the arm low, and 0 of the 71 overhead poses.

A stiffer spring feel at the steep law, unmeasured (also M5). The lobe follower is force-closed by K's clock spring (0.08 N.m + 0.015 N.m/rad, row red_team.liftoff). The wearer feels kK x tau_K at J2. Claim (kK 1.957): 0.18 N.m, 1.2-1.5 N at a 120-150 mm cuff. Ghost law (kK 3.0, K used 54.0 deg = 0.94 rad): 3.0 x (0.08 + 0.015 x 0.94) = 0.28 N.m, 1.9-2.35 N at 150-120 mm: within 0.15 N of the 2.5 N line at a 120 mm cuff, and over it for a lever under 113 mm. K also turns 3x as fast as q2, so the follower's dynamic hold (lift-off under the chain's inertia) matters more. No R17 / dynamics run exists for kK 3.0.

Partly idle stroke on the claim (s65n2d). The drive's range is 65.0 deg. The re-worn bench (exact, model unchanged) records K over taken poses spanning -0.7265 rad = 41.63 deg. That confirms the row's 41.62 and the 'taken poses use 41.6 deg of K' reading. Held out (re-worn, 26.19 reproduced): 41.52 deg. Slipper-nose, the short-stroke leader, uses 45.6 deg on the bench and 46.3 held (remeasure coord_spans). So the long-stroke claim uses 4 deg LESS K than the design it was meant to beat. 23.4 deg of its 65-deg stroke (36 %) is idle on every taken pose, and it pays +8.25 complexity (30.5 vs 22.25). Its cma3 constraint 'stroke >= 65' was met vacuously. The row says this itself, and the claim ranks behind the reference, so nothing is ranked above a better design.
